issues.description: Typo 'stlib' instead of 'stdlib' in the deprecation directive lands in rendered docs.
issues.detail: The .. deprecated:: 4.3 block reads 'Use the stlib's' rather than 'stdlib's'. This renders into Sphinx output that users see when they hit the warning. A trivial fix to make in the same commit since the directive is already being added.

issues.description: Deprecation message should show how to compose both stdout and stderr redirection.
issues.detail: The warning names contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr but doesn't explain that callers using both must nest two context managers (or use ExitStack). One extra clause closing the loop on the both-streams replacement would match the actual decomposition and help migration.

issues.description: Deprecation test does not exercise the stderr substitution path.
issues.detail: The new test only verifies stdout redirection, but the deprecation promises substitutability by both contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr. Adding a stderr case would confirm the full contract being deprecated still holds.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously approves this change as a clean subtraction: a bespoke context manager that complected stdout/stderr redirection is being deprecated in favor of composable stdlib primitives (contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr) that already model the concern correctly. Substitutability and postconditions are preserved, the deprecation path is conservative (warn now, remove in 5.0), and internal tests already migrated. Only cosmetic and documentation polish remain: fix the 'stlib' typo, show the nested-with replacement for the both-streams case, and add a stderr test. Ship after nits.
